Report: Active Transportation And Demand Management for ALDOT
Details: ALDOT will strive to monitor, control, and influence travel and facility demand of the entire transportaion system and dynamically manage a users entire trip throughout all of their mode choices. Multiple choices go into the users trip choice including destination on Choice, Time of Day Choice, Mode Choice, Route Choice, and Lane/Facility Choice. All of these choices can be dynamically impacted by decisions made in real time by ALDOT based on current levels of congestion experienced throughout the system.

Report: AMS Pasadena Testbed – Simulation Results
Details:
This report details the development and application of 
the AMS Chicago Testbed to evaluate Active Transportation and Demand Management (ATDM) and Dynamic Mobility Applications (DMA) strategies. It aims to enhance transportation system performance by improving mobility, safety, and environmental benefits through simulation-based evaluations of various operational strategies under diverse conditions. The study was conducted using data-driven models developed by Northwestern University and supported by the USDOT.

Report: AMS Chicago Testbed and Data
Details:
This report focuses on the AMS Chicago Testbed, 
developed by Northwestern University under the USDOT’s Active Transportation and Demand Management (ATDM) and Dynamic Mobility Applications (DMA) programs. It aims to evaluate and refine strategies to improve mobility, safety, and environmental performance through simulation and analysis of dynamic traffic management techniques and weather-related operations in the Chicago area.

Report: Active Transportation and Demand Management
Details:
This report, developed by the FHWA, outlines 
methodologies and tools for analyzing and implementing Active Transportation and Demand Management (ATDM) strategies. It aims to enhance traffic flow, reliability, and operational efficiency by providing frameworks and examples, such as converting HOV lanes to HOT lanes, to assess the benefits of ATDM investments under various scenarios.
KeyAreas: Conversion of HOV to HOT Lanes

Report:
The Active Transportation and Demand 
Management Program (ATDM): Lessons Learned
Details: This report documents insights and critical issues from implementing ATDM strategies across the U.S. It aims to guide transportation agencies in dynamically managing travel demand, traffic flow, and system performance to improve safety, efficiency, and sustainability​.

Report:
Active Transportation and Demand Management (ATDM)
Foundational Research
Details: This report outlines a framework for evaluating and implementing dynamic traffic and demand management strategies. It aims to enhance system performance through proactive and real-time management, leveraging modeling tools to support planning, design, and operations for improved mobility and safety.

Report: Arterial Management Intelligent Intersections
Details:
This report focuses on leveraging connected vehicle 
technologies and intelligent intersections to enhance traffic signal control, improve safety, and optimize mobility on arterial networks. Developed under the USDOT’s ITS Joint Program Office, it evaluates the benefits, costs, and best practices of deploying cutting-edge Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS).

Report: Arterial Traffic Management Strategies
Details:
This report focuses on arterial traffic management 
strategies aimed at improving traffic flow, accessibility, and transportation efficiency. It provides an overview of various strategies, such as traffic signal management, adaptive traffic control, and dynamic parking systems, highlighting their benefits, prerequisites, and examples of implementation to optimize urban mobility and reduce congestion.

Report:
Arterial Management Plan
Methodology
Details:
This report outlines the methodology for developing 
Arterial Management Plans (AMPs) to enhance the efficiency, safety, and capacity of Virginia's arterial highway network. It aims to guide strategic planning and management of corridors to minimize congestion, support economic development, and accommodate future growth without extensive roadway widening.

Report: Arterial Management
Details:
This report by the FHWA Office of Operations addresses
 strategies for managing traffic on arterial roadways, focusing on traffic signal improvements, advanced control systems, and access management techniques. It aims to enhance traffic flow, reduce congestion, and improve safety by leveraging research, development, and deployment of innovative transportation technologies.

Report:
Active Arterial Management
Traffic Management Center
Standard Operating Guidelines
Details:
This report provides a comprehensive framework for the
 operations of the Orlando Regional Traffic Management Center (RTMC). It aims to enhance traffic management, safety, and mobility on arterial roadways through standardized protocols, Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS), and real-time monitoring strategies to mitigate congestion and improve roadway efficiency in Florida's District

Report: Freeway and Arterial Management Effort (FAME) Research Plan
Details:
This report focuses on developing strategies and 
technologies to enhance the management and operation of freeway and arterial systems. It aims to improve traffic flow, reduce congestion, and integrate innovative solutions to optimize mobility and safety across transportation networks.

Report: Bottleneck Removal
Details: This report focuses on bottleneck removal as a cost-effective strategy to reduce localized congestion and improve traffic flow on highways. It highlights methods such as restriping, lane additions, and ramp modifications, emphasizing their safety and efficiency benefits while addressing implementation challenges. The report aims to guide transportation agencies in mitigating congestion through low-cost, high-impact solutions.

Report: An Agency Guide on How to Establish Localized Congestion Mitigation Programs
Details: This report, developed by the FHWA, provides guidance for state and local agencies on establishing Localized Bottleneck Reduction (LBR) programs. It aims to mitigate recurring, point-specific congestion through low-cost, quick-to-implement operational improvements, offering templates, case studies, and strategies for effective program implementation and evaluation.

Report:
Traffic Bottlenecks: Identification
and Solutions
Details: This report, "Traffic Bottlenecks: Identification and Solutions," focuses on identifying and prioritizing traffic bottlenecks using data-driven methods, innovative tools, and performance measures. It aims to propose cost-effective and practical mitigation strategies to reduce congestion, improve traffic flow, and enhance overall mobility.

Report:
Developing a Systematic Approach to Improving
Bottleneck Analysis in North Carolina
Details: This report, titled "Developing a Systematic Approach to Improving Bottleneck Analysis in North Carolina," aims to create a comprehensive framework for identifying, analyzing, and mitigating freeway bottlenecks at a system-wide level. It uses dynamic traffic assignment models and vehicle probe data to prioritize bottleneck mitigation projects, improve traffic flow, and assist decision-makers in allocating transportation resources effectively.

Report:
Congestion
Pricing: A Primer
Details: This report, Congestion Pricing: A Primer, published by the Federal Highway Administration, explores congestion pricing as a strategy to manage traffic flow, reduce congestion, and optimize roadway efficiency. It outlines the concept, benefits, technological approaches, and real-world examples, aiming to provide a foundational understanding for implementing congestion pricing initiatives effectively.

Report:
Congestion Pricing
A Primer: Overview
Details: The report, "Congestion Pricing: A Primer," by the Federal Highway Administration, provides an overview of congestion pricing as a strategy to manage traffic demand, reduce congestion, and improve transportation system efficiency. It aims to introduce decision-makers and transportation professionals to the concept, its benefits, implementation strategies, and real-world examples from the U.S. and abroad.

Report: Congestion Pricing Basics
Details: This report discusses the concept and implementation of congestion pricing as a tool to manage traffic demand, improve travel time reliability, and generate revenue for transportation projects. It explores the economic, technological, and policy implications of congestion pricing and provides an overview of its applications and impacts in the United States and abroad.

Report:
Congestion Pricing
in New York
Details: This report, developed by the Traffic Mobility Review Board (TMRB), provides recommendations for implementing New York City's Central Business District Tolling Program. It aims to reduce congestion, improve air quality, and generate $15 billion for public transit enhancements by proposing a toll structure that balances equity, simplicity, and environmental justice.

Report: Variable Pricing
Details: This report discusses variable pricing strategies as a tool for managing congestion on roadways by using financial incentives to influence driver behavior. It aims to improve traffic flow, reduce congestion, and enhance transportation network efficiency by implementing time-of-day and dynamic tolling systems, offering insights into best practices and case studies.

Report:
Assessing the Full Costs of Congestion on Surface
Transportation Systems and Reducing Them through
Pricing
Details: This report, prepared by HDR for the U.S. Department of Transportation, evaluates the full costs of surface transportation congestion, including travel delays, unreliability, and environmental impacts. It aims to assess these costs from a national perspective and explore congestion pricing as an effective strategy to improve roadway efficiency and enhance social welfare.

Report: Emergency Transportation Operations
Details: This report outlines the Emergency Transportation Operations (ETO) framework under ALDOT's Statewide TSMO Master Plan, focusing on preparedness, response, and recovery strategies for non-recurring events like natural disasters and emergencies. It aims to enhance inter-agency coordination, optimize evacuation planning, and leverage innovative technologies to ensure safety, mobility, and effective incident management.

Report:
Best Practices in
Emergency Transportation Operations
Preparedness and Response
Details: This report, titled "Best Practices in Emergency Transportation Operations Preparedness and Response," consolidates insights from workshops conducted across 30 U.S. regions between 2002 and 2005. It aims to enhance emergency preparedness, improve interagency coordination, and provide actionable strategies for effective transportation operations during emergencies, focusing on preparedness, response, and recovery phases.

Report:
Common Issues in
Emergency Transportation Operations
Preparedness and Response
Details:
This report, titled "Common Issues in Emergency 
Transportation Operations Preparedness and Response," consolidates findings from 30 workshops conducted by the FHWA and Booz Allen Hamilton between 2002 and 2005. It aims to identify and address critical issues in emergency transportation operations, focusing on interagency coordination, communication, evacuation planning, and the integration of Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS), to enhance preparedness, response, and recovery during emergencies.

Report:
Emergency Transportation Operations
A Major ITS Initiative
Details: This report focuses on the Emergency Transportation Operations initiative under the US DOT's ITS program. It aims to enhance preparedness and response to major incidents like natural disasters and hazardous material accidents through advanced ITS technologies, improving real-time management, resource allocation, and traveler information for safer and more efficient operations​

Report:
Texas department
Of transportation
2023-2024 educational series
Emergency operations
Details: This report, part of TxDOT's 2023-2024 Educational Series, outlines the Texas Department of Transportation's emergency operations strategies and responsibilities. It aims to enhance public safety by detailing TxDOT's roles in disaster preparedness, response, and recovery, including traffic management, debris removal, and interagency coordination during emergencies like hurricanes, wildfires, and severe weather.

Report: Freeway management and Operations
Details: The "Freeway Management and Operations Handbook" serves as an introductory guide for transportation professionals, offering an overview of institutional and technical aspects related to freeway planning, design, operation, and management. It aims to enhance mobility, reduce congestion, improve safety, and incorporate Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) to optimize freeway performance and support emergency operations.

Report: Freeway Corridor Management
Details: This report, "Freeway Corridor Management," provides a comprehensive overview of strategies and practices for optimizing traffic operations and managing congestion within urban freeway corridors. It aims to guide agencies in implementing coordinated management systems, integrating various components like surveillance, traffic control, incident management, and public information to enhance mobility, safety, and efficiency.

Report:
Highway Traffic Operations
And Freeway Management
State-Of-The-Practice
Details: This report, "Highway Traffic Operations and Freeway Management: State-of-the-Practice", provides a comprehensive overview of current practices in freeway management and operations. It aims to identify gaps between state-of-the-practice and state-of-the-art strategies, offering recommendations to enhance traffic flow, safety, and system efficiency through improved technologies and management approaches.

Report:
Operations-Oriented Performance Measures for 
Freeway Management Systems
Details:
This report, titled "Operations-Oriented Performance 
Measures for Freeway Management Systems", explores the development and application of real-time performance measures to enhance freeway management. It aims to evaluate and implement measures such as travel time and congestion extent to support traffic monitoring, incident management, and operational decision-making in Transportation Management Centers (TMCs).

Report: Freeway Management for Optimal Reliability
Details:
This report, titled "Freeway Management for Optimal 
Reliability," explores strategies to enhance freeway travel time reliability through a multi-institutional effort. It develops analytical and simulation-based approaches to assess and optimize Active Traffic Management (ATM) strategies, evaluates their safety benefits, and proposes innovative methods like connected vehicle headway control to improve mobility and reliability
KeyAreas: Integrated ramp metering and variable speed limit control

Report: Assessment of Innovative and Automated Freight and Automated Freight Strategies Strategies and Technologiesnd Technologies—Phase I Phase II Final ReportFinal Report
Details:
This report, titled "Assessment of Innovative and 
Automated Freight Strategies and Technologies—Phase II," evaluates nine freight strategies and technologies to enhance efficiency, safety, and sustainability in Texas' freight systems. Conducted by the Texas A&M Transportation Institute in cooperation with TxDOT and FHWA, it aims to inform strategic investments and future implementations using the STREAM evaluation process.

Report: Texas Freight Network Technology and Operations Plan
Details:
The "Freight Network Technology and Operations Plan" 
is a strategic document developed by the Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) to enhance the safety, efficiency, and mobility of the Texas Multimodal Freight Network (TMFN). It outlines technology-driven solutions and operational strategies to address current and future freight challenges, leveraging emerging technologies, data integration, and stakeholder engagement to support economic growth and improve freight transportation systems
KeyAreas:
Collision avoidance and 
emergency management technologies
Integration of multiple data sources for enhanced decision-making

Report:
Integrated Corridor Management Analysis,
Modeling and Simulation (AMS) Methodology
Details:
This report, titled "Integrated Corridor Management 
Analysis, Modeling, and Simulation (AMS) Methodology," outlines a framework for evaluating and improving transportation corridor operations using Integrated Corridor Management (ICM) strategies. It aims to refine analysis, modeling, and simulation tools to assess and optimize mobility, safety, and operational efficiency across multimodal transportation networks
KeyAreas: Measures the predictability of travel times

Report: Integrated corridor Management (ICM) Demonstration sites
Details:
This report details the U.S. Department of Transportation's
Integrated Corridor Management (ICM) Initiative, highlighting demonstration projects on US-75 in Dallas, TX, and I-15 in San Diego, CA. It aims to improve corridor performance through real-time decision support systems, multimodal coordination, and proactive traffic management strategies to optimize mobility and reduce congestion.

Report:
Integrated Corridor Management (ICM) Program
Major Achievements, Key Findings, and Outlook
Details:
This report provides an overview of the Integrated 
Corridor Management (ICM) Program by the U.S. Department of Transportation, highlighting its key achievements, findings, and future outlook. It aims to demonstrate the benefits of integrated, multimodal corridor management strategies, fostering collaboration among transportation agencies to improve mobility, reliability, and operational efficiency along major travel corridors.
KeyAreas: proactive responses to unplanned incidents or events

Report:
Integrated Corridor Management:
Implementation Guide and Lessons Learned
Details:
The report, Integrated Corridor Management: Implementation Guide and Lessons Learned, provides a comprehensive framework for adopting Integrated 
Corridor Management (ICM) strategies to address congestion and improve travel time reliability in urban corridors. It offers practical guidance, lessons learned, and examples from U.S. Department of Transportation's ICM Pioneer Sites to assist agencies in planning, deploying, and maintaining effective multimodal transportation systems.

Report:
Integrated Corridor Management (ICM) for the 
Lower Hudson Transit Link (LHTL) corridor Program
Details:
This report focuses on implementing Integrated 
Corridor Management (ICM) for the Lower Hudson Transit Link (LHTL) corridor, aiming to optimize traffic flow, improve travel reliability, and enhance safety through strategies like ramp metering, transit signal priority, and real-time travel information. It outlines the benefits of these measures for buses, automobiles, and trucks, contributing to more efficient and safer transportation networks.

Report:
Guidance for Planning, Operating, and Designing 
Managed Lane Facilities in Texas
Details:
This report, titled "Guidance for Planning, Operating, 
and Designing Managed Lane Facilities in Texas," provides a comprehensive framework for the planning, design, operation, and evaluation of managed lanes to enhance traffic flow and mobility. Sponsored by TxDOT and FHWA, it aims to offer preliminary geometric and operational guidelines for managed lane projects, drawing on best practices and experiences from Texas and across the U.S.

Report: Managed Lanes Primer
Details:
The Managed Lanes Primer provides an overview of 
managed lanes as a mobility strategy to address growing traffic congestion. It aims to guide community leaders, policymakers, and transportation managers in understanding managed lanes, their operational strategies, and how they can enhance traffic flow and provide travel options in congested corridors.

Report:
Managed Lanes: A New Concept for Freeway
Travel
Details:
The report "Managed Lanes: A New Concept for Freeway 
Travel" explores the concept of managed lanes as a strategy to optimize freeway traffic flow. It discusses various lane management strategies, such as time-of-day restrictions, vehicle type restrictions, and variable pricing, aiming to enhance travel efficiency, offer more commuter choices, and address congestion challenges in urban areas.

Report: Managed Lanes – Traffic Modeling
Details:
This report, titled "Managed Lanes – Traffic Modeling,
" focuses on evaluating the operational impacts of managed lanes on freeways using the VISSIM simulation tool. Sponsored by TxDOT and FHWA, it aims to analyze design scenarios, optimize traffic flow, and provide recommendations for managed lane access, weaving distances, and traffic management strategies to enhance mobility and efficiency.

Report: Managed Lanes: What They Are and Why We Need Them
Details:
This report provides an overview of managed lanes, 
explaining their definitions, key operational strategies, and applications as outlined by the Federal Highway Administration (FHWA). It aims to clarify misconceptions about managed lanes, highlight their purpose in enhancing traffic flow and congestion management, and present various strategies for implementing and managing these lanes effectively.

Report: Managed Lanes Handbook
Details:
The Managed Lanes Handbook provides a 
comprehensive guide for planning, designing, and operating managed lanes to improve freeway efficiency and mobility. Developed by the Texas Transportation Institute for TxDOT and FHWA, it offers practical strategies and resources to support informed decision-making and effective implementation of managed lanes projects.

Report: Work Zone Operations Best Practices Guidebook
Details:
The "Work Zone Operations Best Practices Guidebook 
(Third Edition)" is a resource developed by the Federal Highway Administration (FHWA) to provide transportation agencies with a compilation of effective work zone management practices. Its aim is to enhance mobility and safety in work zones by sharing strategies, technologies, and policies successfully employed across various states and localities​

Report: Work Zone Management Guidebook
Details:
The Work Zone Management Guidebook by MoDOT 
(March 2021) provides strategies and tools to enhance safety and minimize traffic disruptions in work zones. It outlines advanced work zone strategies, including smart technologies and operational improvements, aiming to protect workers and motorists while optimizing traffic flow during construction activities.

Report: Work Zone Management Program
Details:
This report explores the use of the National 
Performance Management Research Data Set (NPMRDS) is used to assess and manage work zone performance. It aims to provide transportation agencies with tools and methodologies to measure mobility impacts, optimize work zone management strategies, and meet federal requirements for performance monitoring under MAP-21.

Report:
Smart Work Zone Guidelines
Design Guidelines for
Deployment of Work Zone
Intelligent Transportation
Systems (ITS)
Details:
This report, Smart Work Zone Guidelines by TxDOT, 
provides recommendations for incorporating Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) into work zones to enhance safety, mobility, and efficiency. It outlines design, deployment, and evaluation strategies for Smart Work Zones, offering tools and guidelines to standardize and improve their implementation across projects.
KeyAreas: Temporary Incident Detection and Surveillance Systems
